findings.title: Underwater withdraw buffer is FCFS at par, socializing strategy loss onto slow stakers
findings.triageReason: Intended design (confirmed by protocol owner). The underwater buffer pays daily-volume withdrawals at par during transient, mean-reverting underwater dips to avoid sparking panic and to avoid forcing users to realise losses by redeeming shares at the bottom; bank-run / mass-exit is handled separately by migrateOut with pro-rata distribution. The report itself concedes there is no incremental victim (the slow staker is baseline-unchanged vs a no-buffer world). The buffer-at-par path implements the documented invariant 'a non-migrating user cannot be forced to realise a loss', and both of the finding's recommended fixes (block the buffer branch / pro-rata haircut) would defeat that design goal. Reclassified from Medium to intended-design via /review-finding.

findings.title: Terminal migration has no mint-free escape hatch if phUSD minter rights are revoked mid-migration
findings.triageReason: Intended design (user triage 2026-06-08, via /review-finding ss7m3). emergencyWithdraw/withdraw/deposit are deliberately frozen once migrationInfo[token].active because initiateMigration captures an immutable (R,P) snapshot and every exit pays a fixed pro-rata credit p_i*min(R,P)/P; a live exit during migration would mutate P and corrupt the snapshot (StableStaker.sol:306-307, 335-340). The Law-2 'faithfulness gap' framing is therefore invalid. The residual 'revoke staker's phUSD minter while migration active -> exits revert' sliver is an obvious admin misstep (Law 3 out-of-scope) and recoverable. Not submittable.
findings.proposalResolution: REJECTED 2026-06-08 — finding triaged wont-fix as intended design; proposed Medium not applied.
findings.description: During an active terminal migration, emergencyWithdraw is blocked (migration active), and the only exits (userMigrate, batchMigrate) mint frozen pending phUSD via _exitPosition -> phUSD.mint BEFORE transferring principal. If the staker loses phUSD minter rights while a token is active, those exits revert on the pending-phUSD mint and principal is retrievable only after minter rights are restored. Healthy mode has a mint-free escape (emergencyWithdraw); terminal mode does not. Bounded by the owner-trusted precondition 'minter revoked mid-migration'.
findings.impact: Owner-trust-bounded availability: principal is not permanently lost, but is temporarily unrecoverable from terminal-migration exits until phUSD minter rights are restored.

findings.triageReason: Acknowledged (user triage 2026-06-08, via /review-finding ss7m4). Finding is VALID and stays at Medium: the underwater buffer-path withdraw genuinely desyncs totalStaked < strategy.principalOf and bricks initiateMigration's L392 full-drain post-check (PoC passes). Accepted-not-fixed because the clean root fix is CROSS-CUTTING across two submodules: it requires a new client-callable RELINQUISH-PRINCIPAL primitive on the yield strategy (reduce clientBalances[token][client] and totalDeposited by the buffer-paid amount WITHOUT redeeming shares) added to reflax-yield-vault's IYieldStrategy + ERC4626YieldStrategy, plus a stable-staker buffer-branch call into it. This is finding Option A formalized. Beyond un-bricking migration it reconciles principalOf==totalStaked at source AND correctly surfaces post-recovery over-collateralization as skimmable surplus -> yield to stable-yield-accumulator (the relinquished shares stay in the strategy, repurposed from principal-backing to surplus-backing; totalValue unchanged, totalDeposited drops, surplus rises by exactly the relinquished amount). Re point-1 (donation-funded buffer): NOT an exploit vector — a donation lands in the staker's idle balance, never touches the strategy's clientBalances/totalDeposited/totalValue, and relinquish only fires when a real user claim is extinguished, so it cannot be pumped; freed value is honest over-collateralization (at worst spreads to co-clients of a SHARED strategy via pooled accounting, harming no claimholder; avoidable with a dedicated strategy). Re point-3 (par-vs-haircut fairness): already covered — withdraw reverts while underwater except through the reserve buffer (by design), residual FCFS is the wont-fix 'underwater buffer FCFS at par' M and the M-05 emergencyWithdraw family. Fix is design-level/cross-submodule, not a one-line staker patch.
findings.fixVerification: VERIFIED-FIXED at stable-staker-08 (HEAD f85450b). story-007 landed the cross-submodule relinquishPrincipal primitive (declared IYieldStrategy L41, implemented AYieldStrategy._relinquishInternal) and wired the stable-staker buffer branch to call strategy.relinquishPrincipal(token, amount) at StableStaker.sol:703 — reducing principal WITHOUT redeeming shares, so principalOf == totalStaked is preserved through a buffer-path withdraw and initiateMigration's L392 full-drain post-check is once again satisfiable. PoC-replay PoC_M04_BufferDesyncBricksMigration.t.sol LIKELY-FIXED: a migration that previously bricked now succeeds with principalOf == 70 == totalStaked. This was the user's primary audit driver. Owner had acknowledged with the Option-A cross-submodule fix as the accepted path; that fix has now landed, so status flips acknowledged -> fixed with evidence (consistent with the owner's stated intent, not a silent overwrite).

findings.title: setYieldStrategy underwater-swap silently lifts the underwater-withdraw block and FCFS-concentrates the realized loss on the last withdrawer
findings.description: A residual of the story-006 fix. Swapping a token's yield strategy via setYieldStrategy while the OLD strategy is underwater drains only the recoverable principal R_old < totalStaked with the underwater guard OFF (_routeExit(token, totalStaked, false) at L214-217), redeposits R_old into the new strategy at L231-233 (deposit return discarded), and NEVER rewrites pool.totalStaked. The new strategy reads at par, so _isUnderwater (L666-668) is false and withdrawDisabled (L612-617) flips TRUE->FALSE. The pre-swap underwater-withdraw block (which protected non-migrating users from realizing a loss) is silently erased while a real totalStaked - R_old shortfall remains, and the blocked loss is realized FCFS-at-par: early withdrawers paid in full, the last withdrawer absorbs the entire shortfall.
findings.impact: Value leak / concentrated inter-user loss: a routine owner strategy swap performed while the old strategy is underwater lifts the protective block and converts a deferred underwater loss into a concrete FCFS principal loss landed on the last withdrawer. Total payout never exceeds realizable value (no protocol theft). Law-3 non-obvious owner footgun.
findings.rootCauseDistinction: Distinct from same-function siblings via rootCauseClass: NOT dab5a656 (M-01, healthy-pool adoption-haircut desync) and NOT 678e6fa2 (M-02, missing !active guard). Fingerprint dbdc3ac9 does not collide with either.

findings.title: finalizeAndReset revives pool without resetting phusdPerSecond / re-wiring yieldStrategy (revival over-emission footgun)
findings.description: story-009's finalizeAndReset flips poolState Migrating -> Active to revive a fully-drained pool, clearing the migration snapshot and fast-forwarding lastRewardTime, but it does NOT reset phusdPerSecond nor re-wire/clear yieldStrategy. A pool revived without re-configuring its emission rate / strategy resumes on stale settings: the prior phusdPerSecond is re-applied to fresh deposits, and the decoupled (or stale) strategy reference may not match operator intent. The per-second emission CAP is NOT violated and no principal is at risk; the hazard is that a non-obvious owner expectation (a 'reset' pool starts from a clean emission/strategy slate) does not hold.
findings.impact: QA / Law-3 non-obvious owner-config footgun. Emission cap not violated, no principal at risk. Recommend finalizeAndReset zero phusdPerSecond (or require an explicit re-config) and clear/re-assert the yieldStrategy binding on revival.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md Terminal-migration section documents the superseded irreversible active-bool model (story-009 doc-lag)
findings.description: lib/stable-staker/CLAUDE.md Terminal-migration section (L84-96) still documents the irreversible `active`-bool model ('sets active = true ... Migration is terminal: once engaged a token's pool can never resume healthy operation (no resume path)'). story-009 superseded that model with a PoolState enum plus finalizeAndReset (StableStaker.sol ~L585-596), which DOES revive a drained pool (PoolState Migrating -> Active). The documented spec and the code now disagree. Law 2 doc-lag; no security impact (the code is the new intended behaviour, the doc is stale). NB: lib/ is read-only — this is REPORTED, not fixed.
